newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria delays ruling on TSBank insolvency.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria delays ruling on TSBank insolvency.

text.p: The Sofia City court on Friday postponed ruling on an insolvency suit against private Trade & Savings Bank (TSBank) by two months until a report on its financial condition was prepared, a central bank official said.
"The court required an expert ruling on the bank's financial condition and postponed the case until February 17," the official told reporters.
The central bank (BNB) placed TSBank in receivership on September 23 due to a danger of insolvency, dismissing its management and appointing sequestrators to establish its financial state.
On October 31 the BNB initiated a bankruptcy procedure against TSBank which had delayed payments of 4.766 billion levs as of September 20.
The court also rejected on Friday a demand by the bank's sequestrators to put the suit on hold until the Supreme Court ruled on their plea against BNB's decision to place TSBank in receivership.
TSBank sequestrators claimed that putting the bank in receivership was unfounded after it signed a memorandum of understanding with the BNB.

The BNB in June signed memorandums with eighteen local banks, which pledged to improve loan portfolios and boost their capital-to-assets ratio above zero as part of Bulgaria's attempts to meet International Monetary Fund's funding requirements.
TSBank's capital-to-assets ratio was slightly above zero at the end of August.

The BNB has placed 14 or one quarter of Bulgaria's commercial banks in receivership and has so far filed insolvency suits against eight of them in line with pledges made to the International Monetary Fund to close debt-ridden banks in a bid to stabilise the shaky banking sector.

On Tuesday the court postponed ruling on state-owned Mineralbank until March and on Wednesday said it would announce its decision on First Private Bank, Bulgaria's biggest private bank, in 14 days. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 8569
